TÜRKİYE · DAY-END SCORECARD · 11 November 2026
Yesterday the balancing price sat above the day-ahead price in most hours.

🎯 Balancing vs day-ahead: the balancing price was below the day-ahead price in 2 hours, above it in 14, equal in 8.

📊 The day's generation mix (EPİAŞ):
🌞 Solar 9.6% (licensed 2.2% + unlicensed 7.4%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 26.3%
🍃 Wind 14.0%
🔥 Natural gas only 12.7%
🌱 Total renewables 55.0% — all fossil 45.0%

📉 The price (MCP, Market Clearing Price):
🌞 12:00 → 550 TL/MWh, the floor of the day, with solar at 14,661 MWh
🌙 17:00–18:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 48,701 MWh in the first hour
Daily average 3,091 TL/MWh.

From 11:00 to 17:00, the first hour of the ceiling run, demand rose 368 MWh, solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 14,398 MWh, hydro, wind and other renewables added 5,328 MWh and fossil generation added 9,199 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 15,706,556 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Constraint-coded instructions were 73.6 MWh of 18,930 MWh instructed in total. The largest positive hourly cost came at 09:00, an up-regulation hour: on the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to the price cap, above the 4,487 TL/MWh system marginal price (SMP), so day-ahead would have cost more.

📆 Versus 10 November 2026: the daily average price was 19.2% lower and wind generation 193.2% higher.
📆 Versus 4 November 2026, the same weekday one week earlier: the daily average price was 6.7% lower and wind generation 14.4% higher.

💡 What it means:
In Türkiye, how low the day-ahead price falls at midday follows what fossil plants have left to cover, not demand. At 12:00, consumption minus solar, hydro, wind and other renewables was lowest on 11 November, then 18,354 MWh on 4 November and 24,595 MWh on 10 November, the same order as the day-ahead prices at that hour. Demand at 12:00 does not line up: 4 November had the least of the three and still cleared above 11 November. The residual already nets out solar and the other renewables; solar alone, and hydro, wind and other renewables alone, rank the three days in the same order, an equal fit.

Source: EPİAŞ Transparency Platform, 11 November 2026 (retrieved 12 November 2026, 12:26 UTC+3)
